questions.explanation: A lineage generally traces descent from a known common ancestor through a specified line, whereas a clan is often a broader descent group whose members may claim a common ancestor or origin that is not individually traced.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between descent and residence?

options.A: They are the same thing
options.B: Descent determines how ancestry or group membership is traced; residence refers to where a couple or family lives after marriage, such as patrilocal, matrilocal or neolocal residence
options.C: Descent refers to where a couple lives; residence refers to ancestry
options.D: Descent is a marriage rule; residence is a kinship term

questions.explanation: Descent determines how ancestry or group membership is traced; residence refers to where a couple or family lives after marriage, such as patrilocal, matrilocal or neolocal residence.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between education and social change?

options.A: Education prevents all social change
options.B: Education can challenge harmful practices, spread scientific knowledge, increase awareness of rights, develop new skills and support changes in social attitudes, institutions and economic opportunities
options.C: Education has no relationship with social change
options.D: Education only preserves traditions without any change

questions.explanation: Education can challenge harmful practices, spread scientific knowledge, increase awareness of rights, develop new skills and support changes in social attitudes, institutions and economic opportunities.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between religion and communalism?

options.A: Religion politicises identity, while communalism concerns beliefs and rituals
options.B: Religion concerns beliefs, rituals and spiritual or ethical traditions; communalism politicises religious identity in ways that may create antagonism or unequal treatment between communities
options.C: Both are identical concepts
options.D: Communalism is a spiritual tradition, while religion is a political ideology

questions.explanation: Religion concerns beliefs, rituals and spiritual or ethical traditions. Communalism politicises religious identity in ways that may create antagonism or unequal treatment between communities.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between a society and a community?

options.A: A community is a broad system of social relationships, while a society is a more identifiable group
options.B: Society is a broad system of social relationships and institutions among people; a community is generally a more identifiable group connected by locality, shared identity, interests or belonging, and a society can contain many communities
options.C: A society is a type of community
options.D: Society and community are identical concepts

questions.explanation: Society is a broad system of social relationships and institutions among people. A community is generally a more identifiable group connected by locality, shared identity, interests or belonging. A society can contain many communities.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between a community and an association?

options.A: A community is a deliberately organised group with formal membership rules, while an association is connected by belonging and shared identity
options.B: A community is usually connected by belonging, shared identity or common life, while an association is a deliberately organised group formed to pursue specific objectives, often with membership rules and formal structure
options.C: Both are identical concepts
options.D: An association is connected by belonging, while a community has formal membership rules

questions.explanation: A community is usually connected by belonging, shared identity or common life, while an association is a deliberately organised group formed to pursue specific objectives, often with membership rules and formal structure.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between a nuclear family and a joint family?

options.A: A nuclear family includes all relatives, while a joint family includes only spouses and children
options.B: A nuclear family usually comprises a couple and their dependent children, whereas a joint family includes a wider set of related members or generations who maintain shared domestic, economic or family arrangements
options.C: A nuclear family lives in villages, while a joint family lives in cities
options.D: A nuclear family traces descent through females, while a joint family traces descent through males

questions.explanation: A nuclear family usually comprises a couple and their dependent children, whereas a joint family includes a wider set of related members or generations who maintain shared domestic, economic or family arrangements.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between divorce and judicial separation?

options.A: Divorce permits spouses to live apart but does not end the marriage; judicial separation legally dissolves the marriage
options.B: Divorce legally dissolves the marriage; judicial separation permits spouses to live apart but does not itself end the marriage
options.C: Both legally dissolve the marriage
options.D: Both permit spouses to live apart without ending the marriage

questions.explanation: Divorce legally dissolves the marriage; judicial separation permits spouses to live apart but does not itself end the marriage.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between an arranged marriage and a forced marriage?

options.A: An arranged marriage occurs without consent, while a forced marriage involves family participation with consent
options.B: An arranged marriage involves family or community participation in introducing or selecting partners but the individuals' free consent remains essential; a forced marriage occurs without free consent and involves coercion, pressure or threats
options.C: Both involve coercion and lack of consent
options.D: An arranged marriage is illegal, while a forced marriage is legal

questions.explanation: An arranged marriage involves family or community participation in introducing or selecting partners, but the individuals' free consent remains essential. A forced marriage occurs without free consent and involves coercion, pressure or threats.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between consanguineal kinship and affinal kinship?

options.A: Consanguineal kinship is created through marriage; affinal kinship is based on descent
options.B: Consanguineal kinship refers to relationships based on descent or common ancestry; affinal kinship refers to relationships created through marriage
options.C: Both refer to relationships created through marriage
options.D: Both refer to relationships based on descent

questions.explanation: Consanguineal kinship refers to relationships based on descent or common ancestry, such as relationships between parents and children or between siblings. Affinal kinship refers to relationships created through marriage, such as relationships between spouses and between a person and their spouse's relatives.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between formal, non-formal and informal education?

options.A: Formal education occurs through daily life; non-formal education is institution-based; informal education is organised outside the formal system
options.B: Formal education is systematic learning delivered through recognised institutions according to prescribed curricula; non-formal education is organised and purposeful learning outside the regular formal structure; informal education occurs through daily life, family, work, observation, media and personal experience without necessarily following a formal curriculum
options.C: Formal education is organised outside the formal system; non-formal education is systematic learning in institutions; informal education is prescribed curricula
options.D: All three forms of education are identical

questions.explanation: Formal education is systematic learning delivered through recognised educational institutions according to prescribed curricula, stages, assessments and qualifications. Non-formal education is organised and purposeful learning outside the regular formal school or university structure. Informal education is learning that occurs through daily life, family interactions, work, observation, cultural participation, media and personal experience without necessarily following a formal curriculum.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes monotheism, polytheism, atheism and agnosticism?

options.A: Monotheism is belief in multiple deities; polytheism is belief in one God; atheism is the view that God's existence is unknowable; agnosticism is the absence of belief in God
options.B: Monotheism is belief in one God; polytheism is belief in or worship of multiple deities; atheism is the absence of belief in the existence of God or gods; agnosticism is the view that the existence of God or ultimate religious claims are unknown or may be unknowable
options.C: Monotheism is the absence of belief in God; polytheism is belief in one God; atheism is belief in multiple deities; agnosticism is the view that God's existence is unknowable
options.D: All four terms refer to belief in one God

questions.explanation: Monotheism is belief in one God. Polytheism is belief in or worship of multiple deities. Atheism is the absence of belief in the existence of God or gods. Agnosticism is the view that the existence of God or ultimate religious claims are unknown or may be unknowable.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the constitutional Articles with their subject matter regarding freedom of religion?

options.A: Article 25 deals with religious instruction in educational institutions; Article 26 deals with freedom of conscience; Article 27 deals with management of religious affairs; Article 28 deals with taxation for promotion of religion
options.B: Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practise and propagate religion; Article 26 protects the rights of religious denominations to establish and maintain institutions, manage religious affairs and own and administer property; Article 27 protects persons from being compelled to pay taxes specifically appropriated for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion; Article 28 regulates religious instruction or worship in educational institutions
options.C: Article 25 deals with taxation for promotion of religion; Article 26 deals with freedom of conscience; Article 27 deals with religious instruction; Article 28 deals with management of religious affairs
options.D: All four Articles deal with the same subject matter

questions.explanation: Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health and the other provisions of Part III. Article 26 protects the rights of religious denominations or sections thereof to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, manage religious affairs, and own and administer property in accordance with law. Article 27 protects persons from being compelled to pay taxes specifically appropriated for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination. Article 28 regulates religious instruction or worship in educational institutions and provides protections concerning participation or attendance in specified circumstances.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the changing nature of family in India?

options.A: Family structure has remained completely unchanged
options.B: Education, urbanisation, migration, employment, changing gender roles, smaller family size, rising life expectancy and individual choice have influenced family structure, with nuclear households growing in many settings while extended family networks and support often continue
options.C: Only government policies have influenced family structure
options.D: Family structure has changed only in urban areas

questions.explanation: Education, urbanisation, migration, employment, changing gender roles, smaller family size, rising life expectancy and individual choice have influenced family structure. Nuclear households have grown in many settings, while extended family networks and support often continue.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of family in transmitting culture?

options.A: Families only transmit economic resources
options.B: Families transmit language, customs, food practices, religious beliefs, values, stories, traditions and social memory from one generation to another
options.C: Families have no role in transmitting culture
options.D: Families only transmit political beliefs

questions.explanation: Families transmit language, customs, food practices, religious beliefs, values, stories, traditions and social memory from one generation to another.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the concept of consent in marriage?

options.A: Consent of the parents only
options.B: A free and informed agreement to marry; coercion, force, fraud or lack of legally valid consent can affect the validity of a marriage and may attract legal consequences
options.C: Consent of the community only
options.D: Consent of the religious authority only

questions.explanation: Consent means a free and informed agreement to marry. Coercion, force, fraud or lack of legally valid consent can affect the validity of a marriage and may attract legal consequences under applicable law.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of kinship in Indian society?

options.A: Kinship has no role in Indian society
options.B: Kinship can shape marriage alliances, inheritance, family support, caregiving, social identity, ritual duties, residence patterns and networks of cooperation, with influence differing across regions, castes, tribes and religions
options.C: Kinship only determines residence patterns
options.D: Kinship only determines religious practices

questions.explanation: Kinship can shape marriage alliances, inheritance, family support, caregiving, social identity, ritual duties, residence patterns and networks of cooperation. Its influence differs across regions, castes, tribes and religions.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of education in women's empowerment?

options.A: Education has no role in women's empowerment
options.B: Education improves knowledge, skills, economic opportunities, awareness of rights, health-related decision-making and participation in public life, while helping challenge gender-based barriers
options.C: Education only helps women find employment
options.D: Education should be restricted to domestic skills for women

questions.explanation: Education improves knowledge, skills, economic opportunities, awareness of rights, health-related decision-making and participation in public life, while helping challenge gender-based barriers.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of education in national integration?

options.A: Education should promote only one language and culture
options.B: Education can promote constitutional values, common citizenship, respect for diversity, scientific temper, democratic participation and understanding among communities
options.C: Education has no role in national integration
options.D: Education should promote religious division

questions.explanation: Education can promote constitutional values, common citizenship, respect for diversity, scientific temper, democratic participation and understanding among communities.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the State in maintaining religious freedom?

options.A: The State should promote one official religion
options.B: The State must protect freedom of conscience and religious practice, prevent discrimination and violence, maintain public order and ensure that religious freedoms are exercised consistently with constitutional limits and the rights of others
options.C: The State should prohibit all religious practices
options.D: The State should have no role in religious matters

questions.explanation: The State must protect freedom of conscience and religious practice, prevent discrimination and violence, maintain public order and ensure that religious freedoms are exercised consistently with constitutional limits and the rights of others.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of Gram Sabha in community participation?

options.A: It conducts elections to the Lok Sabha
options.B: It provides a village-level forum for registered voters in the Gram Panchayat area to participate in local governance, discuss development priorities and exercise powers assigned by the Constitution and State law
options.C: It issues currency notes
options.D: It maintains law and order in cities

questions.explanation: The Gram Sabha provides a village-level forum for registered voters in the Gram Panchayat area to participate in local governance, discuss development priorities and exercise powers assigned by the Constitution and State law.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of self-help groups in community development?

options.A: They are large government organisations
options.B: They are small voluntary groups, often formed around savings, credit and mutual support, that can strengthen financial inclusion, livelihoods, collective decision-making and women's participation
options.C: They are political parties
options.D: They are religious institutions

questions.explanation: Self-help groups are small voluntary groups, often formed around savings, credit and mutual support. They can strengthen financial inclusion, livelihoods, collective decision-making and women's participation.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes social capital?

options.A: Financial capital owned by the government
options.B: Resources available through social networks, trust, shared norms and cooperation, which can help communities coordinate action and support members, although networks can also exclude outsiders
options.C: Physical infrastructure in a community
options.D: Natural resources in a region

questions.explanation: Social capital refers to resources available through social networks, trust, shared norms and cooperation. It can help communities coordinate action and support members, although networks can also exclude outsiders.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following statements about social institutions is correct?

options.A: They are only relevant to government administration
options.B: They organise recurring patterns of social behaviour, define roles and expectations, meet important social needs and provide continuity to society
options.C: They are temporary arrangements with no lasting impact
options.D: They only exist in traditional societies

questions.explanation: Social institutions organise recurring patterns of social behaviour, define roles and expectations, meet important social needs and provide continuity to society. Family, marriage, kinship, education, religion and community are major institutions or institutional arrangements.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following is a common characteristic of a family?

options.A: Formal membership rules and structure
options.B: Socially recognised relationships, emotional bonds, cooperation, shared responsibilities, socialisation of children, continuity across generations and some form of economic or caregiving organisation
options.C: Government recognition
options.D: Written constitution

questions.explanation: Common characteristics include socially recognised relationships, emotional bonds, cooperation, shared responsibilities, socialisation of children, continuity across generations and some form of economic or caregiving organisation. Family forms vary across societies.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following is a main element of religion?

options.A: Only sacred texts
options.B: Beliefs, rituals, symbols, sacred texts or traditions, moral codes, religious specialists, places of worship and communities of believers
options.C: Only places of worship
options.D: Only moral codes

questions.explanation: Common elements include beliefs, rituals, symbols, sacred texts or traditions, moral codes, religious specialists, places of worship and communities of believers. Not every religion has all elements in the same form.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Which of the following is a main characteristic of a community?

options.A: Formal membership rules and structure
options.B: A sense of belonging, social interaction, shared interests or identity, norms, mutual support and some degree of continuity
options.C: Government recognition
options.D: Written constitution

questions.explanation: Common characteristics may include a sense of belonging, social interaction, shared interests or identity, norms, mutual support and some degree of continuity. A community need not always occupy one geographical area.

questions.subject: Social Institutions
questions.question: Who is associated with the concept of the family as a universal social institution in comparative sociology?

options.A: Emile Durkheim
options.B: Talcott Parsons
options.C: George Peter Murdock
options.D: A. R. Radcliffe-Brown

questions.explanation: George Peter Murdock is well known for comparative studies of family structures and functions. His conclusions are influential but have also been debated by later scholars.
